blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever uma resenha de um livro sobre ética das virtudes, equilibrando elogio e crítica, com ritmo adequado.

body: Esta aula treina **escrever frases claras e corretas (IELTS Writing, TOEFL Writing)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Review: “Becoming Good” by Rafael Ibarra (fictional)
paras: Ibarra’s study of virtue ethics asks how **character** is **formed** rather than which rule to follow. Drawing on Aristotle, he argues that **courage and temperance** are **cultivated by practice**, **much as** a pianist is made by scales. **Where the book excels** is in its **case studies**: a nurse, a referee, a negotiator, each **facing** a moral choice with no rule to hand.

**Where it falters** is in the middle chapters, **which lean heavily on** a single example. **Nor does it adequately address** the charge that virtues vary across cultures. **Still**, the prose is **warm** and the **argument**, if **not airtight**, is **persuasive**. **Recommended** for readers who prefer **portraits** to **principles**.

items.q: Ibarra focuses on rules rather than character.
items.why: how character is formed rather than which rule.

items.q: The reviewer finds the middle chapters strong.

blocks.body: **Where… is** é uma pseudoclivada de lugar. **Nor** + auxiliar + sujeito obriga a **inversão**: *Nor does it address*. Faça uma **pausa** antes de *Still,* para marcar a virada.
*Principle* (princípio) ≠ *principal* (diretor, principal). Pronúncia igual /ˈprɪnsəpəl/ vs. /ˈprɪnsəpəl/ — atenção à grafia!

items.s: ___ the book excels is in its case studies. (where)
Nor ___ it adequately address the charge. (do)
Virtues are cultivated ___ as a pianist is made. (much)
The argument, if not ___ , is persuasive. (airtight)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Where it falters.** — Onde falha.
**Nor does it…** — Tampouco…
**Much as…** — Assim como…
**Warts and all.** — Com todos os defeitos.
**Walk the walk.** — Praticar o que prega.
**Practise what you preach.** — Praticar o que se prega.
**A cut above.** — Um nível acima.
**Strike a balance.** — Equilibrar.
**Golden mean.** — Meio-termo.
**By and large.** — De modo geral.
**Where does the book excel?** — Onde o livro se destaca?
**And where does it falter?** — E onde ele vacila?
**Nor does it address cultural variation adequately.** — Também não trata adequadamente da variação cultural.

items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence review of a book, film or restaurant, with a strength (Where… excels), a weakness (Where… falters) and a Nor-inversion.
blocks.model: Where the restaurant excels is in its bread. Where it falters is the service, which is slow. Nor does the menu offer much for vegetarians. Still, the atmosphere is warm and the prices fair. If not flawless, it is memorable. Recommended for a quiet lunch.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
